chunks: Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Saʿd narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

Al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās said: A mule was presented to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله by Kisrā or Qayṣar. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله rode it with a covering of hair, and seated me behind him. Then he said to me:

O young boy, safeguard Allah, and He will safeguard you. Safeguard Allah, and you will find Him before you. Come to know Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in ease, and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The Pen has already passed with what is to be. If people were to strive to benefit you with something Allah has not written for you, they would not be able to do so. And if they were to strive to harm you with something Allah has not written against you, they would not be able to do so. So if you are able to act with patience alongside certainty, then do so; and if you cannot, then be patient, for indeed in patience over what you dislike there is much good. And know that victory is with patience, relief is with distress, and with hardship comes ease.

key_terms.احْفَظِ اللَّهَ: Guard Allah’s limits and commands, and remain faithful to His obedience.
key_terms.الرَّخَاءِ: Times of ease, comfort, and well-being.
key_terms.الصَّبْرِ: Sabr; patient perseverance in the face of difficulty.
key_terms.الْقَلَمُ: The Pen, referring here to what has already been decreed and written.

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله teach about trusting Allah, patience, and divine decree?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches reliance upon Allah, turning to Him alone in asking and seeking help, and maintaining awareness of Him in both ease and hardship. It also emphasizes divine decree, sabr, and yaqīn, concluding with the assurance that victory and relief come through patience and that hardship is accompanied by ease.
